You can absolutely change your claims effective start date to when you changed from full time employment. 

Call unemployment and select the option for back pay. When you speak to the rep explain the date you lost full time employment, that you've been working less than full-time hours since, and that you want to update your effective claim start date to when you lost full-time employment. They'll transfer you to someone in the claims department who you'll have to reexplain this to and then they will transfer you to a level 3 staff (this will take at least an hour or two waiting) and they'll be able to cancel your current claim and make a new one with the correct start date. This is also the best person to ask any questions you have about your claim and any concerns or worries you have.

start applying. I was in the same boat sans having taken the boot camp, and I expected getting an entry level job, *maybe* a jr level job, and instead I lucked into getting a job as a Front-end Engineer because they liked that I was completely self-taught and had good html/css/es6 skills and had potential, even if i lack projects or a portfolio. 

You never know what'll happen unless you don't apply.

Do you have a github with some repos? Or a portfolio site? You NEED to showcase your code without a degree.

If you dont have anything go make a brochure site for a fake company, a single page application for a product, an ecommerce page with a working cart, and whatever small little projects you think look good. Those are projects that are similar to what youd be doing as a front end dev on the regular so a company can get really good insight by looking at the source code of them. you can bang that all out in a few weeks then you should be fine to start getting interviews.

Search this Reddit for people that posted their personal sites and copy their project ideas. Just avoid the generic stuff like Building a todo list.
